raw:
{
  "need": "Competence",
  "secondary": { "name": "Status", "description": "The public nature of a customer catching the error makes this feel like a reputation hit, not just a technical slip — they're protecting against looking incompetent again." },
  "read": "They are not being lazy or difficult — they are trying to guarantee they never feel that exposed again. Triple-checking is a survival response: their internal story is that they are someone who ships mistakes, and they are trying to disprove it by eliminating all risk. The problem is that eliminating risk has become the goal, and the work is suffering for it.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Enforcer", "instinct": "Push them to speed back up and point out that the over-checking is now its own performance problem — which confirms their fear that they cannot get it right either way and drives them further into the spiral." },
  "mentorMove": "Validate that the error stung and that caring about quality is exactly right, then reframe the overcorrection as a sign of a capable person recalibrating — not a person who is broken — while being honest that the current pace is a standard you need them to get back to together.",
  "holdFirm": [
    "Delivery velocity is a real job requirement, not a nice-to-have — the team depends on their output and customers depend on timelines.",
    "The standard is quality AND throughput; neither one gets dropped."
  ],
  "stayFlexible": [
    "They get to decide what their review checklist looks like — build it with them, not for them.",
    "They can choose where in the workflow they front-load their checking so it does not bottleneck every step."
  ],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 3, "label": "Collaboration" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, got a few minutes? I want to check in — not about the error itself, we moved past that, but about how things have been feeling since. I noticed the pace has slowed down quite a bit and I wanted to talk about it with you, not at you." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "What is going on in your head when you are reviewing your work right now? Walk me through what the process feels like. I am asking because I think what I am seeing on the outside does not tell the whole story." },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here is what I think is happening, tell me if I am off: one error got through, a customer saw it, and now some part of your brain has decided the only safe move is to check everything twice as long. That makes complete sense as a response — it is actually your instincts working. The problem is it has overcorrected past what is actually useful. Can we build something together — a real checklist or a defined review step — so you have a system you trust instead of just checking until the anxiety goes down?" },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I need you back at full pace — that is not negotiable because the team genuinely needs it and because I think you are capable of it. I am holding you to that standard precisely because I have watched your work and I know you can deliver quality at speed. One error does not change that read. What I want from you this week is one concrete thing we can put in place so you feel like you have a real safety net, not just nerves." }
  ],
  "longGame": "Once pace recovers, give them a small stretch assignment where they are the one who reviews someone else's work — it shifts them from someone trying to avoid failure to someone whose judgment is trusted, which is the status repair this moment actually needs."
}
situation: A junior shipped something with a mistake a customer caught, and now they are triple-checking everything and velocity has cratered.
